alexcrichton opened PR #14683 from alexcrichton:optimize-ref-func to bytecodealliance:main:

This PR is a series of commits which ends up optimizing the ref.func implementation within Wasmtime to notably not require a hostcall and additionally not require any function lookups within the compiled function tables. There's a number of linked issues to poor performance of ref.func and while this isn't a truly "zero cost" implementation it is significantly faster than it otherwise is today. The same implementation as before, where the fields are unconditionally initialized, is used no matter what. Conditional initialization could be part of a later runtime refactoring, if needed.

Note: this is a draft PR since there's an open design question around the Cranelift side of things I'd like to discuss this coming Wednesday.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

I've a thread on Zulip about why this isn't optimizing
:memo: fitzgen submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

I don't think this is something that can be inferred, because that would require determining whether a given function call writes to the location (or alias region) in question.

I think we may want to, in the limit of time, annotate signatures with the set of alias regions they use (and maybe, in the fullness of time, split that into observe vs mutate), but that is a bit separate from this TODO I think.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

"the this"

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

This is going to lose whether the field is aligned or not, for example. I think this should instead be something like

let flags = self.flags_with_region(cursor.func).with_readonly(false);

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

Can the new relocations be added in a separate PR, just to help split this up and make it easier to review?

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

doc comment needs fixing

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Unfortunately the core change here can't land without this since otherwise tests on aarch64/riscv64 will fail. I can land the change for relocations separately, but then they're not tested until this lands. I split them out into separate commits for this PR, but if you'd like I can land them ahead of time on main

Do you think it's worth having this comment at all? I tried to capture some of the Cranelift meeting discussion in this, but you're right that actually removing the need for this would be a pretty ambitious project
